Genomic data filters

Contemporary means a reported collection year after 1930. Worldwide counts include records needing biological review. Regional candidates pass the date, coordinate and biological screens in the Atlantic–Caribbean–Gulf window. These species-level filters are independent of the historical stage and region filters.

Species trait filters

Combine traits with the sampling filters above. Different fields must all match. Water types and habitat tags test membership in positive records; an unlisted tag is not evidence of absence. Missing or withheld values remain visible until an active trait filter excludes them.

Reported maturity age — minimum (years)
Reported maturity age — maximum (years)

Shallowest reported depth (m)
Deepest reported depth (m)
Maximum reported length (cm)

A minimum exceeds its maximum. Correct the range to show matching species.

Model ages and reported ages are separate fields. Trophic level prefers the diet estimate, then food items; methods are not averaged. Source-specific feeding classes and reef guilds remain separate. Missing traits do not mean biological absence. IUCN categories are dated source snapshots, not verified latest status. Lengths take the largest reported value across sexes separately for each type; TL, SL and FL are not converted. Numeric bounds apply to the named summary field, not to all population-level observations.

Filters determine which of the 80 eligible species can be selected. Specimen/year thresholds use dated records through 1930 across all life stages within the chosen region. Trait and genomic filters select species. Only the separate map life-stage control changes the plotted data; maps retain all included regions and years, including undated lots.

    No species match these filters. Reset or relax the filters to select a fish.

    Fixed extent: 100–50°W, 5–60°N · 2° cells. Hatching marks approximate positions. Adult / non-larval includes juveniles and unlabeled lots; maturity is unverified.

    Colors count specimens, not abundance, and use one scale across life stages within the selected species. Blank cells mean no plotted sampling. Approximate positions are display estimates, not verified sites.
